=====================================System Note: The sub-agent EXHAUSTED its budget and failed to reach a conclusion. WARNING: This does NOT mean the method is bug-free. If your static analysis strongly suggests the bug is here, YOU MAY re-nominate this method using DIFFERENT 'target_lines' or 'verification_goal'."

The buggy method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.processObjectLitProperties(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.ObjectType)`

Diagnosis:
- The failing tests are both about typed-percent accounting on object literal keys.
- `TypeCheck` counts an object literal key as typed only if the key node itself has a non-null, non-unknown `JSType`.
- In `visitObjLitKey`, the key type comes from `getJSType(key)`. If the key node was never assigned a type earlier, it becomes `UNKNOWN`, lowering the typed percentage.
- For normal object literals, `TypedScopeCreator.defineObjectLiteral` delegates to `processObjectLitProperties`, which computes `keyType`.
- But `processObjectLitProperties` only assigns that type to the key node when the key has no qualified name:
  - if `qualifiedName != null`, it calls `defineSlot(...)`
  - else it calls `setDeferredType(keyNode, keyType)`
- Object literal keys like `a = {TRUE: 1, FALSE: 0};` do have a qualified name (`a.TRUE`, `a.FALSE`), so they skip `setDeferredType(keyNode, keyType)`.
- As a result, those key AST nodes themselves remain untyped even though the property may be declared in scope/object type metadata.
- This exactly explains the undercount:
  - `testGetTypedPercent6`: 2 untyped keys out of 6 counted nodes gives `4/6 = 66.666...`
  - `testGetTypedPercent5`: 3 untyped enum keys similarly account for the reduced percentage.
- The enum case is affected through the same underlying issue: enum/object-literal property keys are not reliably getting a `JSType` attached to the key nodes that `TypeCheck` later counts.

Best fix location:
- Ensure `processObjectLitProperties(...)` always assigns the computed `keyType` to the `keyNode` itself, even when there is a qualified name and `defineSlot(...)` is called. That keeps the AST node typed for percent accounting while preserving existing property/slot declarations.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

m47.content:
The buggy method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.processObjectLitProperties(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.ObjectType)`

Diagnosis:
- The failing tests are both about typed-percent accounting on object literal keys.
- `TypeCheck` counts an object literal key as typed only if the key node itself has a non-null, non-unknown `JSType`.
- In `visitObjLitKey`, the key type comes from `getJSType(key)`. If the key node was never assigned a type earlier, it becomes `UNKNOWN`, lowering the typed percentage.
- For normal object literals, `TypedScopeCreator.defineObjectLiteral` delegates to `processObjectLitProperties`, which computes `keyType`.
- But `processObjectLitProperties` only assigns that type to the key node when the key has no qualified name:
  - if `qualifiedName != null`, it calls `defineSlot(...)`
  - else it calls `setDeferredType(keyNode, keyType)`
- Object literal keys like `a = {TRUE: 1, FALSE: 0};` do have a qualified name (`a.TRUE`, `a.FALSE`), so they skip `setDeferredType(keyNode, keyType)`.
- As a result, those key AST nodes themselves remain untyped even though the property may be declared in scope/object type metadata.
- This exactly explains the undercount:
  - `testGetTypedPercent6`: 2 untyped keys out of 6 counted nodes gives `4/6 = 66.666...`
  - `testGetTypedPercent5`: 3 untyped enum keys similarly account for the reduced percentage.
- The enum case is affected through the same underlying issue: enum/object-literal property keys are not reliably getting a `JSType` attached to the key nodes that `TypeCheck` later counts.

Best fix location:
- Ensure `processObjectLitProperties(...)` always assigns the computed `keyType` to the `keyNode` itself, even when there is a qualified name and `defineSlot(...)` is called. That keeps the AST node typed for percent accounting while preserving existing property/slot declarations.
